findings.title: Blocked-email matching is case-sensitive
findings.body: This lookup compares the submitted email string exactly with the stored value. Email addresses are commonly treated case-insensitively, but a user can submit a differently cased local part or domain (for example, `Blocked@EXAMPLE.COM`) and avoid a blocklist entry stored as `blocked@example.com`. Normalize the address consistently before lookup and when storing blocked entries.

findings.title: Validation increments the match counter more than once per signup
findings.body: Calling `should_block?` has a database write side effect, but Rails validations can run multiple times for one attempt. In particular, `UsersController#create` calls `user.valid?` and then `user.save`, which validates again; a blocked signup therefore increments `match_count` twice. Keep validation side-effect-free or record the match once per signup attempt.

findings.title: Concurrent matches can lose counter increments
findings.body: The counter is updated with a read-modify-save sequence. If two requests load the same `match_count` before either saves, both write the same incremented value, so one match is lost. This makes the blocked-email statistics undercount during concurrent attempts; use an atomic database increment or locking.
